message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on highways with 2–3 lanes each direction, 35 mph on 4‑lane highways, 25 mph on 5‑lane highways.
• School zones: 20 mph (or 15 mph if a school bus is present). | Texas Transportation Code §545.02 | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat belt law” for drivers over 18, but all passengers must buckle. | Texas Transportation Code §545.04 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers 21+.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.05, 545.06 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is a moving‑violation offense. | Texas Transportation Code §545.07 | | **Headlights & Signal Use** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning or changing lanes. | Texas Transportation Code §545.01 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on the right.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Texas Transportation Code §545.03 | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in front of a driveway or on a sidewalk.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.09 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Drivers must not pass a stopped school bus until the bus’s stop sign is down and lights are off. | Texas Transportation Code §545.02 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.10 | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., Sam Houston Tollway, LBJ Freeway).
• Toll rates vary by vehicle type and time of day. | TxDOT Toll Roads website | | **Emergency Vehicle Lanes** | • Do not block emergency lanes.
• Use them only when necessary and obey signage. | Texas Transportation Code §545.01 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) *Contains current statutes, road conditions, and safety campaigns.* 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Accessible online via the Texas Legislature’s website: [https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/) *Search for specific sections (e.g., §545.05 for DUI).* 3. **Local County Courts** – For recent changes or local ordinances that supplement state law. 4. **Legal Aid & Law Libraries** – Many universities and public libraries offer free access to legal resources. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s the simplest way to reduce injury risk. - **Avoid distractions** – put your phone on “Do Not Disturb” mode while driving. - **Observe speed limits** – they’re designed for safety and are strictly enforced. - **Check for school zones** – especially during school start/end times. - **Use headlights** – even on clear days; visibility is key. - **Stay informed** – traffic laws can change; keep up with TxDOT updates. Feel free to let me know if you need deeper details on any specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
